title: Debts after death - consumer basics
facts: A deceased person's debts generally become obligations handled through the estate rather than automatically becoming the personal debts of relatives.

A surviving person can still be responsible when they were already legally liable, such as a co-borrower, joint account holder under applicable law, or in other circumstances created by state or federal law.
Debt collectors contacting survivors remain subject to applicable federal debt-collection rules.
Who must pay estate debts and the order of payment are heavily affected by state probate law.
